title: Lung cancer is not only about smoking: Doctor explains the risks hiding in your air, home and daily routine
desc: A lung cancer diagnosis can bring a question that is difficult to answer: could anything have been done differently? The answer is not always simple. Smoking is the biggest preventable risk factor, but it is not the only one. Some people who have never smoked also develop lung cancer. Family history, secondhand smoke, radon, air pollution and certain workplace exposures can all play a role. The World Health Organization estimates that lung cancer caused about 2.5 million new cases and 1.8 million deaths worldwide in 2022, making it the leading cause of cancer death globally. It also notes that a substantial number of cases are preventable, with tobacco smoking accounting for the majority of preventable cases.That makes prevention less about finding one magical food or supplement and more about reducing the exposures that repeatedly put lung cells under stress.Dr Anil Kamath, Senior Consultant Surgical Oncology, Apollo Hospitals Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, puts the issue into perspective: “In my years seeing patients, few moments carry as much weight as delivering a diagnosis of lung cancer. Almost every time, the conversation turns to one heavy question: ‘Could I have done something to stop this?’”There may not always be a clear answer after someone develops cancer. But before a diagnosis, several meaningful steps can reduce risk. And some of them are surprisingly ordinary.
